title: Shackleton Gives Wild His Only Biscuit
text:
In January 1909 Ernest Shackleton and three companions, Frank Wild, Eric Marshall and Jameson Adams, were man-hauling their sledge back across the Antarctic ice after turning around less than a hundred miles from the South Pole. They had cut their rations to the bone to stretch the food between depots, and every man was starving.

Wild fell ill with dysentery and could barely keep going. On 31 January, at breakfast, Shackleton pushed his own single biscuit onto Wild and insisted he eat it. It was the one solid piece of food each man got that morning, and Shackleton would march all day without it.

Wild recorded the moment in his diary that night. He wrote that he did not suppose anyone else in the world could fully realize how much generosity and sympathy that act showed, and added: "I DO by God I shall never forget it. Thousands of pounds would not have bought that one biscuit."

He did not forget. Wild went south with Shackleton again on the Endurance expedition as his second in command, and it was Wild who held twenty-two men together on Elephant Island in 1916 while Shackleton sailed for help. He was with Shackleton on his last expedition too, and took command of it when Shackleton died aboard ship in 1922.
lesson: People remember who looked after them when it cost something. A small sacrifice at the right moment can earn a loyalty that no salary or title can buy.
source: Frank Wild, diary of the Nimrod expedition, 31 January 1909 (Scott Polar Research Institute); quoted in Roland Huntford, Shackleton (1985)
